title: THE GROUP-SCALE AMPLITUDE: the r^-1 dust law at 1e13 -- a_c(M500) run to the groups, the f_gas rise test, and the two-parameter dust law across 1e13-9e14
context: G122's closed form (p = +0.99 r^-1, q = -0.41 amplitude run, 0.097/0.119-dex closure); G107's pooled f_gas rise +0.235 +/- 0.039; G125's group sample (GEMS + E11 26 groups) and its r_M/R500 footings; G098's f_dust medians (the dust is a profile, G098 V2 FAIL = flat is excluded).

data_notes.groups: E11 (Eckmiller+11 A&A 535, A105; arXiv:1109.6498 v2) Table 3 + gas-mass block, 26 Chandra groups, transcribed this run from the arXiv HTML; UNVERIFIED-in-repo; transcription gated against G125's committed E11 rows (24 shared, 0 mismatches); internal gates: f_gas = M_gas/M500 and r2500 = R500(M2500/M500)^{1/3}5^{-1/3} for 26/26
data_notes.clusters: committed X-COP ingests + G105 T(r) cache; G107 and G122 recipes reproduced in-lane with gates (pooled +0.235 +/- 0.039; q = -0.414, p = +0.990, rms 0.119/0.097; amplitudes digit-for-digit)

gates.reading: the cluster value the group rise is compared against, reproduced on the committed ingests

gates.reading: the MEASURED amplitude run (not fitted per-cluster): q ~ -0.41 with its honest 12-point error; p-value 0.045 is the significance

gates.name: V1 [the group-scale f_gas shape vs the prediction] the group two-point rise is same-or-steeper than the cluster value
gates.measured: mean = +0.536 +- 0.069 vs +0.235 (20/26 above; cluster two-point mean +0.263)
gates.reading: THE GROUP-SCALE f_gas SHAPE vs THE PREDICTION (same or steeper than the cluster +0.235): MEASURED mean +0.536 +- 0.069 (median +0.609, n = 26, r2500-R500 two-point, E11; 20/26 above +0.235; vs the cluster two-point mean +0.263 over the SAME window).  The group rise is 2.3x the cluster value -> PASS (steeper, as the amplitude run predicts)

gates.name: V2 [the combined 2-parameter dust law with errors] the law and its errors, clusters + groups pooled statement
gates.reading: THE COMBINED 2-PARAMETER DUST LAW WITH THE ERRORS: c_dust = 0.72 x (M500/8e14)^q x (r/R500)^-p with q = -0.41 [-0.57, -0.26] (12 committed amplitudes, Spearman rho = -0.59, p = 0.04; pooled 96-bin q = -0.41 +- 0.09), p = 0.99 [+0.96, +1.03] (r^-1 within errors), c0 = -0.14 +- 0.03; residual floor 0.119 / 0.097 dex; group anchors: rise +0.54 (median +0.61), f_gas(R500) level run +0.34 +- 0.21 dex/dex across 1e13-9e14

gates.name: V3 [the honest statement] ONE free-dust envelope law across 1e13-9e14 -- the thorn's final form
gates.measured: HONEST: the free-dust envelope is ONE LAW across two decades of mass (M500 ~ 1e13-9e14): the shape (r/R500)^-0.99 (the framework's own r^-1) and the amplitude run (M500/8e14)^(-0.41) are now BOTH MEASURED -- 0.119-dex (3-param) / 0.097-dex (13-param) closure at cluster scale, and the group-scale rise +0.54 vs +0.235 + the f_gas(R500) drop (+0.34 dex/dex) verify the same law 1.5 dex down in mass.  The thorn's freedom is reduced to TWO numbers (c0, q) plus the 0.1-dex residual floor; the group data are UNVERIFIED-in-repo (transcribed from E11, gated against G125, internally consistent), the window difference (groups: two-point r2500-R500 vs clusters: 0.2-1.0 R500 OLS) is stated, and the geometric premise of the brief (r_M a LARGER fraction of R500 at group scale) is FALSE on both G125 footings -- the steeper rise is carried by the AMPLITUDE RUN, not by the r_M fraction; the combined 38-system mass trend of the rise (d s/d log M500 = -0.14 +- 0.05, Spearman rho = -0.42, p = 0.01) IS significant while the group-only trend is not (Spearman rho = -0.16, p = 0.42, n = 26) -- the steepening is carried by the cluster-to-group contrast.
gates.reading: the amplitude run is MEASURED at both mass ends; what remains open is the 0.1-dex residual floor and the physical origin of q (the 'what sets q' question), not the law's form

prediction.law: log10 c_dust = c0 + q log10(M500/8e14) + p log10(r/R500)

r_M_footings.premise: r_M is a SMALLER fraction of R500 at group scale on both footings (G125) -- the steeper-rise prediction rests on the amplitude run
